items.title: FromSoftware-Style Bosses Could Stop Being Learnable, As PlayStation's October 1 AI Patent Rewrites Enemy Behavior On The Fly
items.excerpt: New PlayStation patent details an AI system that rewrites NPC behavior dynamically, revolutionizing action and soulslike games like Dark Souls.
items.rationale: New Sony patent filing (Oct 1) for AI that rewrites enemy behavior at runtime. It goes straight at how encounter and boss design gets authored and tuned.

items.title: Retro platformer series Dizzy is back for a new game from its original creators, who are really happy for you to know it's made with AI
items.excerpt: Retro egg-rolling platformer Dizzy is on its way back from the 80s, but with the caveat of its creators being very happy to use genAI for the entire production.
items.rationale: New game announcement: the original Oliver Twins creators are openly making a legacy-IP game end to end with genAI. It is a rare pro-disclosure case and a contrast to the usual backlash.

items.title: After 12 years, Ultra Street Fighter IV gets not one, but two connection-stabilising rollback netcode mods aaaand they're both made using Claude
items.excerpt: Two new mods adding connection-stabilising rollback netcode to Ultra Street Fighter IV appear, but both are made with generative AI.
items.rationale: Two newly released mods use Claude to add rollback netcode, which is hard engineering work, to a 12-year-old fighter. It is a concrete marker of what AI-assisted coding now does to legacy games.

items.title: D&D and Magic The Gathering developers unionize, allege Wizards of the Coast is pushing "adoption of LLMs and generative AI"
items.rationale: New union filing in which management pushing LLM and genAI adoption is a stated reason to organize. It is a new labor-vs-AI flashpoint after the Blizzard AI contract (09-12).

items.title: Sega won't "entrust the creative aspect of games to AI," but is using tech to "improve efficiency" in other departments
items.excerpt: Senior executive officer and deputy chief business officer Tsuyoshi Saito said Sega is "very cautious" about how it implements generative AI during development
items.rationale: Sega's first stated genAI policy: no AI in creative work, AI for efficiency elsewhere. It sits next to Capcom's opposite stance (10-05) as a major-publisher line on where AI is allowed.

This is the GPT-6 Astra StarCraft showdown published 2026-09-30 (36kr). It was already dropped on 10-05 and 10-06. (3) PC Gamer Warhorse co-founder 'AI is not a get out of jail free card'. These are more remarks from the same co-founder interview run covered 2026-09-26 (PC Gamer), so it is commentary, not a new event. Not picked on merit (ranked alternates): Road to VR Astro Bot Quest 3 vibe-coded mod (a third AI-mod card next to USF4), GamesRadar Analogue Pocket SNES AI hack (another vibe-code backlash after 10-03 and 10-05), Wccftech DOOM DLSS 5 port (a heavily covered DLSS 5 mod run), Polygon 'Hell is breaking loose' (opinion round-up of the mashup and jailbreak stories already published), GameMeca National Assembly AI content forum (9/30, policy talk). Diversity: 4 outlets (RPS x2, Wccftech, GamesRadar+, GI.biz). The topics split into a platform patent, an AI-made game announcement, an AI-built mod release, a labor filing and a publisher policy.
